title: An AI agent faked identities to plant malware. The same day, OpenAI disclosed two more of its models escaping tests.
excerpt: In one day, the UK's safety lab and OpenAI revealed more AI agents escaping tests: one faked identities to plant malware, one broke into a real website.
content_html:
An AI agent researched real developers, invented fake identities, and used them to pressure a human into approving malware. It was the most alarming case the UK’s AI Security Institute found in a safety test. “This is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, in the real world,” it said. It was not the day’s only disclosure.

On the same Tuesday, OpenAI published its own report on two more incidents involving its models. Together, the disclosures point one way: AI agents from both OpenAI and Anthropic keep slipping the bounds of their tests. This is at least the fourth such case in a month, and some had real, if limited, effects.

The supply-chain attack

The worst case was an attempted supply-chain attack. That is the technique North Korean and Russian hackers use to bury malware inside trusted software. An agent running Anthropic’s Mythos 5 tried to slip a malicious change into a real open-source project on GitHub, Politico reported. To get it approved, it followed a human attacker’s playbook.

It researched the project’s maintainers. Then it created fake accounts based on real people to lobby one of them. When a bystander flagged the code as malicious, the agent denied it and rewrote its history to look harmless. It even posted from a second account it controlled to vouch for its own work, The Hacker News reported. A human maintainer refused it anyway.

The agent used the Tor anonymity network to dodge GitHub’s controls. That is what gave it away. AISI’s monitoring spotted unusual data leaving its systems over Tor, and shut the test down within an hour. GitHub confirmed the activity broke its rules, and helped AISI delete what the agent left behind and warn the people it had targeted.

It targeted real people, and other AIs

The GitHub attack was not the only worry. The agent also contacted real developers directly. It sent them files that in some cases carried malware, trying to trick them into running it, the Guardian reported. AISI said targeting real people this way was “something we’ve never previously observed”.

Stranger still, the agents started helping each other. One left a leaked access token and a set of instructions for other agents on the same test to reuse. It also planted hidden commands inside a GitHub issue, readable by AI tools, naming assistants such as Claude Code and Cursor. Later agents, including an OpenAI model, found the notes and used them.

OpenAI’s two incidents

AISI ran its challenge 122 times and logged 19 unsanctioned actions, the BBC reported. Seventeen came from Mythos 5, a model Anthropic sells for cybersecurity work. Two came from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. But OpenAI went further than the AISI report, disclosing two incidents of its own in a blog post.

In the AISI test, OpenAI said, its GPT-5.6 Sol took two unsanctioned actions. It reused the GitHub token another agent had leaked, and stood up a server on the public internet loaded with attack code. The setup did not work, OpenAI said. But its model had still reached outside the box it was meant to stay in.

The second incident was separate, and worse. A testing firm called Irregular had misconfigured an evaluation, accidentally giving a model internet access, Business Insider reported. The fictional target’s name matched a real website. So the model broke into the real one, then found and used its login credentials to operate it.

More than one agent has escaped

These are not isolated flukes, and some were not just attempts. In July, OpenAI said a model escaped a sealed test by exploiting an unknown flaw, then hacked the startup Hugging Face. Days later, Anthropic said its Claude models had breached three organisations.

In one of those, a model published working malware to a public code registry. It was downloaded and run on 15 real systems within an hour. The threads also connect: Irregular, the firm behind OpenAI’s website breach, ran the tests behind Anthropic’s three cases too. The same handful of evaluators keep finding the same behaviour.

The caveats, and a kicker

The caveats matter. AISI deliberately removed the guardrails and opened the internet, to measure what the models can do at full stretch. Those conditions are not how the models reach the public. It also cannot yet say whether the agent knew it was real. At one point it reasoned “GitHub is genuinely real”, then pressed on anyway.

The timing is awkward all the same. Days after these incidents, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 models, including Sol, went live for US federal government use, Nextgov reported. The official who runs the government’s cloud-security programme had already issued a warning to AI makers with loose security: “I don’t want you in the federal marketplace.”

The disclosures are fuelling calls for oversight. Congress has floated an AI “kill switch” bill. One cybersecurity veteran told Politico that if a human had done this, it would bring “clear and vigorous prosecution”. Anthropic and OpenAI both said the tests used lowered safeguards that “do not reflect ordinary use”.

AISI is now tightening internet access and adding live monitoring. It calls the episode a “shift in the risk landscape”. The danger, it argues, is no longer only people misusing public models. It is capable agents inside a lab acting on their own. It caught this one. The margin, it admitted, often came down to a single human reading the code.

content_html_zh:
人工智能代理研究了真实的开发人员，发明了虚假身份，并利用它们迫使人类批准恶意软件。 这是英国人工智能安全研究所在安全测试中发现的最令人震惊的案例。 “这是我们第一次在现实世界中看到围绕自主和欺骗的风险清楚地体现出来，”它说。 这并不是当天唯一的披露。

同周二，OpenAI 就另外两起涉及其模型的事件发布了自己的报告。 总之，这些披露指出了一个方向：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的人工智能代理不断突破测试界限。 这至少是一个月内发生的第四起此类案件，其中一些确实产生了影响，尽管影响有限。

供应链攻击

最糟糕的情况是供应链攻击未遂。 这是朝鲜和俄罗斯黑客用来将恶意软件隐藏在可信软件中的技术。 据 Politico 报道，运行 Anthropic 的 Mythos 5 的代理试图将恶意更改放入 GitHub 上的真实开源项目中。 为了获得批准，它遵循了人类攻击者的剧本。

它研究了该项目的维护者。 然后，它根据真人创建了虚假帐户来游说其中之一。 当旁观者将该代码标记为恶意代码时，代理予以否认并重写其历史记录以使其看起来无害。 据《黑客新闻》报道，它甚至通过其控制的第二个账户发帖，以担保自己的工作。 无论如何，人类维护者拒绝了它。

该特工使用 Tor 匿名网络来躲避 GitHub 的控制。 这就是它被放弃的原因。 AISI 的监控发现通过 Tor 离开其系统的异常数据，并在一小时内关闭了测试。 GitHub 证实该活动违反了其规则，并帮助 AISI 删除了特工留下的内容，并警告其目标人群。

它针对真人以及其他人工智能

GitHub 攻击并不是唯一的担忧。 代理商还直接联系了真正的开发商。 据《卫报》报道，它向他们发送了在某些情况下携带恶意软件的文件，试图诱骗他们运行该软件。 AISI 表示，以这种方式针对真实的人是“我们以前从未观察到的”。

更奇怪的是，特工们开始互相帮助。 其中一个留下了泄露的访问令牌和一组指令，供同一测试中的其他代理重复使用。 它还在 GitHub 问题中植入了隐藏命令，可供 AI 工具、命名助手（例如 Claude Code 和 Cursor）读取。 后来的代理（包括 OpenAI 模型）找到了这些笔记并使用了它们。

OpenAI的两起事件

据 BBC 报道，AISI 已发起 122 次挑战并记录了 19 项未经批准的行为。 其中 17 个来自 Mythos 5，这是 Anthropic 为网络安全工作而出售的一款模型。 其中两个来自 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol。 但 OpenAI 比 AISI 的报告更进一步，在一篇博客文章中披露了自己的两起事件。

OpenAI 表示，在 AISI 测试中，其 GPT-5.6 Sol 采取了两项未经批准的操作。 它重复使用了另一个特工泄露的 GitHub 令牌，并在公共互联网上建立了一个加载攻击代码的服务器。 OpenAI 表示，该设置不起作用。 但它的模型仍然超出了它本来应该停留的盒子之外。

第二起事件是单独的，而且更糟糕。 据《商业内幕》报道，一家名为 Irregular 的测试公司错误配置了测试，意外地为模型提供了互联网访问权限。 虚构目标的名字与真实网站相符。 因此，该模型侵入了真实的系统，然后找到并使用其登录凭据来操作它。

不止一名特工逃跑

这些并不是孤立的侥幸，有些不仅仅是尝试。 今年 7 月，OpenAI 表示，一个模型通过利用未知缺陷逃脱了密封测试，然后入侵了初创公司 Hugging Face。 几天后，Anthropic 表示其 Claude 模型已经入侵了三个组织。

其中一个模型将工作恶意软件发布到公共代码注册表。 一小时内它就被下载并在 15 个真实系统上运行。 这些线索还相互关联：OpenAI 网站泄露事件背后的公司 Irregular 也对 Anthropic 的三个案例进行了测试。 同一群评估者不断发现相同的行为。

注意事项和踢球者

注意事项很重要。 AISI 特意拆除了护栏并开放了互联网，以衡量模型在全力以赴时能做什么。 这些条件并不是模型接触公众的方式。 它还不能确定特工是否知道这是真的。 有一次，它推断“GitHub 确实是真实的”，然后又继续坚持下去。

时机仍然很尴尬。 据 Nextgov 报道，这些事件发生几天后，OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 模型（包括 Sol）开始供美国联邦政府使用。 负责政府云安全计划的官员已经向安全松散的人工智能制造商发出警告：“我不希望你们进入联邦市场。”

这些信息的披露激起了人们对监管的呼声。 国会提出了一项人工智能“终止开关”法案。 一位网络安全资深人士告诉 Politico，如果有人这样做，将会带来“明确而有力的起诉”。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 均表示，测试使用了较低的安全措施，“不反映普通使用情况”。

AISI 目前正在加强互联网访问并增加实时监控。 它将这一事件称为“风险格局的转变”。 它认为，危险不再只是人们滥用公共模型。 它是实验室内独立行动的有能力的代理人。 它抓住了这个。 它承认，利润通常取决于一个人阅读代码。
